> How is this base16? A base16 theme would output only the 4-bit ansi color codes to allow the terminal's colorscheme to apply. The base16 standard is about having a more semantic shared understanding of what those colors mean between the application producing them and the terminal rendering them to ensure together they produce something readable.
> 
> And really base16 is too limiting, I would love to have a [base24 colorscheme](https://github.com/tinted-theming/base24/blob/main/styling.md) for opencode, since that gives the various "grayscale" colors that are important for the UI components like the sidebar.
> 
> But AFAICT both base16 and base24 are impossible with opencode right now as it translates 4-bit/256-color ansi color codes into truecolor codes using [an internal mapping table](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/2f32f2ceb59176d9708d13dd132d2491c6f1db51/packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/context/theme.tsx#L233).

@Nemo157 

Thank you for the thoughtful feedback!

I agree that, in terminal-centric base16 workflows, themes often output ANSI color codes and let the terminal supply the colors, but that isn't required by the base16 “philosophy.” Many base16 themes for editors (like VSCode or Vim in GUI mode) use the palette’s hex values directly, mapping base00–base0F to UI slots without relying on the terminal.

This PR maps all theme slots to the official [base16 default palettes](https://github.com/tinted-theming/schemes), following the [semantic slot mapping from the spec](https://github.com/tinted-theming/home/blob/main/styling.md), and avoids “random” hardcoded hex values—so it matches the usual approach for base16 support in GUI apps.

I agree that supporting user-supplied terminal base16 colors would be ideal for true terminal theming (and would require outputting ANSI codes instead of truecolor), but for now, the goal here is to bring spec-compliant color structure and easy extensibility for both dark and light modes, as is typical for base16 themes in editors/GUI apps.

Happy to help discuss or plan support for real terminal-driven base16 in the future (which would be more involved)! For now, this PR ensures the theme matches the official base16 palette semantics.

I agree it could be a context-related problem, but I suspect it’s context size interacting with enterprise infra rather than a pure “context bug”.

In my environment (VM inside big enterprise network → corp proxy → Azure API GW → AWS Bedrock), /compact often makes it work again, which suggests we’re crossing some threshold (longer time-to-first-token, longer stream duration, bigger request/response) that increases the chance the proxy/gateway chain closes the connection. That then surfaces as ECONNRESET / “socket connection was closed unexpectedly”.

So my working theory is: larger context/output increases stream length and/or latency, and somewhere in the proxy/GW path (timeouts, buffering, SSE/chunked handling, HTTP2↔HTTP1.1 translation) the connection gets terminated. 

That would explain why it’s correlated with context growth but also why it can still happen in smaller/fresh sessions depending on network/gateway conditions.
